sentences.text: Eoazhdarcho possessed very elongated metacarpals, the long bones of the hand, while its neck vertebrae and hind legs remained standard in length.

Chinese paleontologists Lü Junchang and Ji Qiang named the genus Eoazhdarcho in 2005, establishing the single known species Eoazhdarcho liaoxiensis. Fossils were found in the Aptian-age Lower Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation in Chaoyang, Liaoning, China. The species name liaoxiensis refers to the ancient region of Liaoxi.
In 2008, the clade containing Eoazhdarcho was named Chaoyangopteridae, which is the sister group to Azhdarchidae within Azhdarchoidea.
A 2018 analysis by Longrich and colleagues placed Eoazhdarcho as a basal member of the clade Neopterodactyloidea within Neoazhdarchia.
In 2025, Thomas and McDavid recovered Eoazhdarcho within the newly named subfamily Shenzhoupterinae.
This animal lived during the Aptian stage, from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
